
# Align-fastqs test fixtures
These fixtures are synthetic micro-fixtures for fast, deterministic tests of the align-fastqs workflow.

They are intentionally small and hand-checkable. Running `make.sh` from `env_protocol` regenerates the fixture set deterministically.

Regenerate fixtures from the repository root with:
```bash
source activate env_protocol
bash tests/fixtures/align_fastqs/make.sh
```

Generated fixture outputs are ignored by Git. When required inputs are missing, `tests/run_tests.sh` regenerates this fixture set automatically.

The fixture set focuses on single-end and paired-end Bowtie 2 alignment to BAM and CRAM output, plus BWA MEM, BWA ALN, and bwa-mem2 MEM alignment to BAM output. These fixtures are not derived from real sequencing data. The reference sequence and FASTQ records are encoded directly in `make.sh` so that the expected read alignments are easy to inspect.

<br />

## Expected alignment behavior
The single-end FASTQ fixture contains one read:

| Read name        | Sequence                         | Expected reference |
| :---             | :---                             | :---               |
| `tiny_se_read_1` | `ACGTTGACCGTTAACGATCGTAGCTAGGAT` | `I`                |

Bowtie 2, BWA MEM, BWA ALN, and bwa-mem2 MEM should align this read to chromosome `I` in the tiny reference. Tests should verify that wrapper-generated BAM/CRAM files and indexes exist, pass `samtools quickcheck`, report or count one read alignment on `I`, and contain the expected read name. CRAM checks should read with `samtools view -T reference/tiny.fa`.

The paired-end FASTQ fixtures contain one read pair:

| Read name        | Mate | Sequence                         | Expected reference | Expected start |
| :---             | :--- | :---                             | :---               | :---           |
| `tiny_pe_pair_1` | R1   | `ACGTTGACCGTTAACGATCGTAGCTAGGAT` | `I`                | 17             |
| `tiny_pe_pair_1` | R2   | `CCTTAGCCGATTAGCCTAAGCTTGATCCGG` | `I`                | 70             |

R1 matches chromosome `I` in forward orientation. R2 is the reverse complement of positions 70-99 on chromosome `I`, so Bowtie 2, BWA MEM, BWA ALN, and bwa-mem2 MEM should report the pair in FR orientation. Tests should verify that wrapper-generated BAM/CRAM files and indexes exist, pass `samtools quickcheck`, report or count two read alignments on `I`, contain the expected paired read name, and include proper-pair flag records when the aligner reports stable proper-pair flags. CRAM checks should read with `samtools view -T reference/tiny.fa`.

<br />

### Repeat fixtures
`make.sh` writes one 150-base repeat and four 400-base unique blocks literally. It then joins them into the 2,050-base reference `chrR`, where three copies of the repeat separate the unique blocks. A read wholly in the repeat therefore has three equally good placements. The 100-base reads are cut from the blocks:

| Read name | R1                                            | R2     | In single-end input |
| :---      | :---                                          | :---   | :---                |
| `chim`    | 60 bases of repeat, then 40 of unique block 3 | unique | yes                 |
| `rchm`    | 60 bases of unique block 3, then 40 of repeat | unique | yes                 |
| `half`    | wholly in the repeat                          | unique | no                  |
| `ctrl`    | unique                                        | unique | yes                 |

With BWA MEM and bwa-mem2, `chim` R1 is a split read with its primary record in the repeat. `rchm` R1 is a split read with its supplementary record in the repeat. The mates of `half` get different MAPQs from these aligners and from BWA ALN. Bowtie 2 writes no supplementary records. `test_align_fastqs_mapq_template.sh` checks the MAPQs each aligner writes before relying on them.

The queryname-copy reads are three 50-base pairs from 300-base fragments of `chrR`. The fragment of `uniq` starts at zero-based offset 50. `dup_a` and `dup_b` are one fragment at offset 1,200 under two names, so duplicate marking marks one of them. R1 is the fragment's first 50 bases on the forward strand. R2 is the reverse complement of the fragment's last 50 bases.

In the SAM fixtures, template `sec_keep` has primary records at MAPQ 60 and a secondary record at MAPQ 0. Template `sec_drop` has a primary record at MAPQ 0 and a secondary record at MAPQ 255. A filter at MAPQ 30 that judges primary records keeps `sec_keep` with its secondary record and drops `sec_drop`. Template `unal_mate` has an aligned R1 and an R2 flagged unaligned (0x4) whose partner lacks 0x8. This is the shape `bwa sampe` writes in #75. The single-end file holds one unaligned read (`unal`). Both unaligned records keep MAPQ 60, so the filter must drop them by their flag rather than their MAPQ.

<br />

### Tie fixtures
`make.sh` runs `make_tie.py`, which draws the tie reference and reads through `random.Random(0).random()`. Python guarantees that stream across versions, so the data are random in content but identical on every run and every host. The reference has two chromosomes, `chrT1` and `chrT2`. Each chromosome holds three 3,000-base unique blocks. A copy of one shared 600-base repeat follows each block, and a 1,000-base unique block ends the chromosome. A read inside a repeat copy has six equally good placements, and Bowtie 2 picks one with a per-read random generator. The reads are 1,000 pairs of 50-base mates cut from 150- to 400-base fragments on either strand. About 30% of mates carry one mismatch.

The same reads come under three header forms. Bowtie 2 seeds each read's generator from its sequence, its qualities, its whole FASTQ header line, and `--seed`. For a pair, it combines the two mates' seeds by exclusive or. That cancels every term the mates share:

| Files     | R1 header                | R2 header                | Change from the row above |
| :---      | :---                     | :---                     | :---                      |
| `tie_pe`  | `tie_<n>`                | `tie_<n>`                |                           |
| `tie_cmt` | `tie_<n> 1:N:0:AAAAAAAA` | `tie_<n> 2:N:0:AAAAAAAA` | the mates now differ      |
| `tie_idx` | `tie_<n> 1:N:0:CCCCCCCC` | `tie_<n> 2:N:0:CCCCCCCC` | a change both mates share |

The single-end files `tie_se` and `tie_cmt_se` hold the R1 reads with the `tie_pe` and `tie_cmt` headers.

Measured with Bowtie 2 2.5.5 and the pipeline's default paired-end call, about 164 of the 2,000 paired-end records and 144 of the 1,000 single-end records are tied (MAPQ 0 or 1). A record moves when its flag, reference, position, MAPQ, CIGAR, or mate fields change. About 136 paired-end records move from `tie_pe` to `tie_cmt`, and none move from `tie_cmt` to `tie_idx`. Changing `--seed` moves no paired-end record but about 123 single-end ones. `--seed 0` gives the same output as no `--seed`. With `-p 8`, the records match those of `-p 1` but come in a different order. `--reorder` restores the `-p 1` order. With BWA-MEM (0.7.19) and BWA-MEM2 (2.3), changing `-K 100000000` to `-K 10000` moves 2 paired-end records because insert sizes are estimated per batch. The whole set is smaller than one default batch, so the thread count alone moves none.

<br />

### Bridge fixtures
`make.sh` joins the repeat fixtures' unique blocks into two contigs: `chrA` (blocks 0 and 1, 800 bases) and `chrB` (blocks 2 and 3, 800 bases). The 100-base pairs are cut from them:

| Read name | R1                       | R2                                                                           |
| :---      | :---                     | :---                                                                         |
| `brdg`    | unique in `chrA`, at 501 | reverse complement of the last 70 bases of `chrA` and the first 30 of `chrB` |
| `ctrl`    | unique in `chrB`         | unique in `chrB`                                                             |

With BWA ALN (0.7.19), `bwa sampe` flags `brdg` R2 unaligned (0x4) but keeps its position. It leaves R1's mate-unaligned flag (0x8) clear, so a per-record `samtools view -F 12` keeps R1 alone. BWA MEM and bwa-mem2 MEM align R2 in part and write a supplementary record on `chrB`. Bowtie 2 end-to-end leaves R2 unaligned and flags R1's mate unaligned. Bowtie 2 local aligns R2 in part. `test_align_fastqs_unaligned.sh` checks the raw BWA ALN flags before relying on them.

<br />

### Pairs fixtures
`make.sh` runs `make_pairs.py`, which draws the pairs reference and reads through `random.Random(0).random()` as `make_tie.py` does. The reference has two chromosomes of random unique sequence. `chrP1` is 6,000 bases and holds copies of one 300-base repeat at zero-based offsets 1,000, 2,500, and 4,000. `chrP2` is 3,000 bases. Each 50-base pair belongs to one class (offsets are zero-based leftmost positions of each mate's alignment):

| Read name    | R1                    | R2                             | Class                         |
| :---         | :---                  | :---                           | :---                          |
| `pair_conc`  | forward, `chrP1` 100  | reverse, `chrP1` 350           | concordant, 300-base fragment |
| `pair_ovlp`  | forward, `chrP1` 500  | reverse, `chrP1` 520           | mates overlap                 |
| `pair_cont`  | forward, `chrP1` 700  | reverse, 30 bases, `chrP1` 720 | R2 contained in R1            |
| `pair_far`   | forward, `chrP1` 4400 | reverse, `chrP1` 5850          | 1,500-base fragment           |
| `pair_dove`  | forward, `chrP1` 1500 | reverse, `chrP1` 1490          | dovetailed                    |
| `pair_rf`    | reverse, `chrP1` 1700 | forward, `chrP1` 1950          | outward-facing (RF)           |
| `pair_ff`    | forward, `chrP1` 2000 | forward, `chrP1` 2200          | same orientation (FF)         |
| `pair_chrs`  | forward, `chrP1` 3000 | reverse, `chrP2` 500           | different chromosomes         |
| `pair_one`   | forward, `chrP1` 3300 | random                         | one mate unaligned            |
| `pair_none`  | random                | random                         | both mates unaligned          |
| `pair_rpt`   | forward, `chrP1` 2550 | reverse, `chrP1` 2850          | R1 in the repeat              |
| `pair_conc2` | forward, `chrP2` 1000 | reverse, `chrP2` 1200          | concordant                    |

With Bowtie 2 2.5.5's default paired-end call (`--no-mixed --no-discordant -X 1000`), the concordant, overlapping, contained, and repeat pairs align concordantly (mate rescue places `pair_rpt`). Every other pair is written with both mates unaligned (flags 77 and 141). With the relaxed call (`-I 0 -X 1000`), `pair_far`, `pair_dove`, and `pair_chrs` are discordant. `pair_rf` and `pair_ff` keep their orientations. `pair_one` has its R1 aligned (73 and 133). BWA MEM (0.7.19) cannot estimate insert sizes from so few pairs, so it flags no pair as proper. It aligns every mate that the relaxed call aligns. `test_align_fastqs_unal_mode.sh` checks the side file's read names per call against these.

The filled set holds the twelve pair classes under the same names and 300 concordant filler pairs (`fill_000` to `fill_299`). The filler pairs lie in the unique blocks away from the repeat copies, and their fragments are 200 to 300 bases. Each filler pair starts at its own position, so none is a duplicate. `make_pairs.py` draws nothing at random for this set, so the other sets are unchanged. With the fillers, BWA MEM and bwa-mem2 MEM estimate insert sizes and flag pairs proper. They flag every filler pair proper, and also `pair_conc`, `pair_ovlp`, `pair_cont`, `pair_rpt`, and `pair_conc2` (99 and 147). They leave `pair_far`, `pair_dove`, and `pair_chrs` improper (97 and 145). They also leave `pair_rf` (81 and 161) and `pair_ff` (65 and 129) improper. `pair_one` (73 and 133) and `pair_none` (77 and 141) are as in the pairs set. `test_align_fastqs_unal_mode.sh` checks that BWA flags at least 600 records proper before relying on them.

The single-end file holds `se_uniq` (forward, `chrP1` 200), `se_uniq2` (reverse, `chrP2` 2000), `se_rpt` (in the repeat), and `se_none` (random).

The duplicate set's names carry flow-cell coordinates (`A00123:8:HFLOWCELL:1:1101:<x>:<y>`). Its first pair is concordant on `chrP2`, with R1 at 1500 and x and y of 1000. The other five pairs have an aligned R1 and a random R2 that does not align. One R1 aligns at the first pair's R1 (x and y of 20000). Two align at 2200 and lie far apart on the tile. Two align at 2600 and lie 100 pixels apart in x and y. With BWA MEM and `--unal_mode separate`, `samtools markdup` marks three of these R1s. It marks the one at the first pair's R1 as a duplicate of that R1, one of the two at 2200 as a library duplicate, and one of the two at 2600 as an optical duplicate.

`sam/split_template_pe.sam` holds these templates on two references (`chrS` and `chrS2`):
- `t75` has an aligned R1 and an R2 flagged unaligned (0x4) whose partner lacks 0x8. This is the shape `bwa sampe` writes (#75). `supp` is the same with a supplementary record for R1.
- `pair` is a complete pair. `lone` is an aligned R1 with no R2 record.
- `ffpp` is a same-orientation (FF) pair flagged proper. `xchr` is a pair flagged proper whose mates map to different references. `bwa sampe` writes such a pair when its mates fall on either side of a chromosome boundary ([lh3/bwa#460](https://github.com/lh3/bwa/issues/460)). `samtools fixmate` unflags both, so `--req_flg` rejects them after `fixmate`.
- `lowq` is a proper pair with one mate at MAPQ 0. `ffmq` is a same-orientation pair flagged proper with both mates at MAPQ 0, so it fails both `--req_flg` and `--mapq`. `disc` is a pair the aligner did not flag proper.

Each template in `sam/diag/` stands for one `.diag.tsv.gz` case when the files are read at MAPQ 30 and a Bowtie 2 `-X` of 500:
- Main file:
  - `m1` is a pair with a secondary record.
  - `m2` is a pair flagged duplicate.
- Side file:
  - `u_both` has both mates unaligned.
  - `u_one` has an unaligned R2 and an aligned R1 flagged duplicate.
  - `u_t75` has the #75 shape: an unaligned R2 and an aligned R1 whose mate-unaligned flag (0x8) is clear.
- Improper file (its primary records carry `MC` as `samtools fixmate -m` writes it):
  - `i_xr` has both mates forward on different references.
  - `i_ff` has both mates forward.
  - `i_rr` has both mates reverse.
  - `i_rf` has its mates facing outward.
  - `i_dov` is dovetailed: its reverse mate starts before its forward mate, and a deletion makes both end at the same base.
  - `i_dov_fe` is dovetailed the other way: both mates start at the same base, and the forward mate ends after the reverse mate.
  - `i_q10` spans 510 bases and has one mate at MAPQ 10.
  - `i_q30` spans 210 bases. Both its mates are at MAPQ 30 (the threshold), and it has a supplementary record at MAPQ 0.
- Low-MAPQ file:
  - `q_low` has one mate at MAPQ 5 and a secondary record.
- Statistics:
  - `all.markdup.txt.gz` counts 3 primary duplicate records (both records of `m2` and the R1 of `u_one`).
  - `all_neg.markdup.txt.gz` holds totals these SAM files cannot produce. Its duplicate total (0) is below the side file's one duplicate record, though its primary total still leaves the main file an even count (2).
  - `all_odd.markdup.txt.gz` holds totals these SAM files cannot produce. Its primary total leaves the main file an odd count (1).

<br />

### Thread fixtures
`make.sh` runs `make_thr.py`, which draws the thread reference and reads through `random.Random(0).random()` as `make_tie.py` does. The reference `chrH` is 100,000 random bases. The 120,000 pairs of 50-base mates come in two blocks. The first holds 100,000 pairs from 190- to 210-base fragments, and one in every 50 of them is replaced by two random reads that do not align. The second holds 20,000 pairs from 590- to 610-base fragments. Each pair is on either strand.

Without `-K`, BWA-MEM (0.7.19) reads 10,000,000 bases per batch per thread and estimates insert sizes per batch. At one thread, the long pairs fill their own batch and are flagged proper. At three threads, one batch holds both blocks, and the long pairs are not flagged proper. Measured: 118,000 proper pairs at one thread and 98,000 at three. With the pipeline's `-K 100000000`, one batch holds every pair at any thread count, and the 20,000 long pairs are improper. So under `--unal_mode separate --req_flg`, a batch that followed the thread count would move them between the alignment file and `<stem>.improp.bam`. Bowtie 2 needs about 25 seconds for the set at one thread. Its final files do not depend on `--reorder` because the coordinate sort fixes their order.

<br />

## Current and deferred test coverage
The test suite covers submit- and execute-layer single-end and paired-end alignment, a local Bowtie 2 GNU Parallel path gated by `RUN_PARALLEL=1`, and a remote Slurm submission path gated by `RUN_SLURM=1`. Set `WAIT_SLURM=1` with `RUN_SLURM=1` to poll for expected Slurm outputs.

`#TODO`: Consider extending GNU Parallel coverage to additional aligners and CRAM output where that broader matrix provides useful regression protection.
